description: Severity distribution for pressure energy release — compressed gas, hydraulic, pneumatic, vacuum, and high-pressure injection events. Distinct from explosion (rapid deflagration/detonation) and thermal (steam burns covered under thermal). Pressure mechanism covers the mechanical energy of pressurised fluid/gas release: whipping hoses, high-pressure injection injuries, pneumatic discharge, compressed gas cylinder failures. P(death) scale from AIS mortality data.
assumptions: No pressure relief, isolation, or guarding
Steam thermal effects are under thermal mechanism — this covers the mechanical pressure energy
magnitude_note: Pressure severity depends on pressure × volume × medium (gas vs liquid). Gas expands on release (blast/whip), liquid doesn't but can inject through skin at high pressure. Bands by scenario because the injury mechanism shifts with pressure and medium.

magnitude_bands.description: Low-pressure pneumatic or air system (<10 bar). Compressed air line, air tools, tyre inflation. Can cause air injection through skin or eye injury at close range.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: Industrial injury data: compressed air injuries are mostly eye/ear/skin. Fatal air embolism from compressed air entering wound or body cavity is documented but rare.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Low-pressure air causes localised injuries. P90=medical_treatment reflects compressed air to eye or ear (tympanic rupture). Fatal air embolism from directed compressed air into wound is documented but requires specific conditions. Tyre explosions (truck/earth-mover) are a separate, higher-severity scenario.

magnitude_bands.description: Tyre/wheel explosion during inflation or servicing. Split-rim, multi-piece wheel, over-inflation. The tyre itself becomes a pressure vessel. Truck and earthmover tyres store enormous energy.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: OSHA tyre explosion fatality data; mining tyre safety bulletins. Split-rim wheel explosions during inflation are a well-documented SIF mechanism. A truck tyre at 8 bar contains enough energy to be lethal at close range.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Tyre explosions combine blast pressure with high-velocity projectile (rim components, tyre fragments). A truck tyre at 8 bar failing explosively produces blast + struck-by simultaneously. P50=serious_injury from blast/fragment injuries. P90=fatality from direct hit by rim component or close-range blast. Cages and remote inflation are the key mitigations.

magnitude_bands.description: High-pressure hydraulic fluid injection (100-700 bar). Pinhole leak in hydraulic hose, grease gun, fuel injector. Fluid penetrates skin and spreads through tissue planes. Deceptively serious — entry wound looks minor.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: Plastic surgery and hand surgery literature: high-pressure injection injuries have ~50% amputation rate for digits. Fatal from sepsis or compartment syndrome if not surgically debrided within hours. Houghton & Varley (1996); Wieder et al. (2005).
magnitude_bands.rationale: High-pressure injection through skin looks like a small puncture but fluid tracks along tissue planes, causing compartment syndrome, tissue necrosis, and sepsis. ~50% of digit injections result in amputation. P50=serious_injury reflects the high amputation/surgery rate. P90=0.50 reflects limb-threatening injection with delayed treatment. Rarely directly fatal but serious injury is the norm.

magnitude_bands.description: High-pressure gas release (>10 bar). Compressed gas cylinder failure, pipeline rupture, pressure vessel safety valve failure, pneumatic accumulator. Whipping hoses, gas jet, blast.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: BOC/Air Liquide cylinder safety data; pipeline rupture incident reports; OSHA pressure vessel fatality data. Gas cylinder rocket/fragment from valve failure is a known killer.
magnitude_bands.rationale: High-pressure gas release produces multiple hazards: whipping hose (struck), gas jet (penetrating), blast (overpressure), cylinder rocket (projectile). A gas cylinder with a sheared valve becomes a projectile. P50=serious_injury from hose whip or gas jet. P90=fatality from cylinder rocket or close-range pipeline rupture.

magnitude_bands.description: High-pressure water jet (100-3000 bar). Water jetting, hydroblasting, waterjet cutting. Can cut through steel — will cut through flesh instantly. Used in industrial cleaning, demolition, cutting.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: WaterJet Technology Association safety data; OSHA waterjet fatality reports. At >1000 bar, water cuts through any biological tissue. Fatalities from hydroblast contact are well-documented.
magnitude_bands.rationale: High-pressure water at >1000 bar cuts through steel — human tissue has no chance. Even glancing contact causes deep laceration. Direct contact with torso causes penetrating injury. P50=serious_injury from limb contact (deep tissue damage, possible amputation). P90=fatality from torso/head contact. Similar injury profile to hydraulic injection but with larger wound.

medium.description: Multiplier on P(death). Hydraulic oil injection causes chemical tissue damage on top of mechanical. Toxic fluids (solvents, fuels) add systemic toxicity. Water is slightly less damaging to tissue than oil.

body_region.description: Multiplier on P(death). Injection/jet injuries to digits cause amputation but rarely death. Torso/head contact with high-pressure jet or blast is frequently fatal.

sources.author: Houghton & Varley
sources.relevance: High-pressure injection injuries — review of outcomes. ~50% amputation rate for grease gun injuries to fingers.

sources.author: OSHA
sources.relevance: Pressure vessel and compressed gas safety data. Cylinder failure and tyre explosion fatalities.

sources.author: WaterJet Technology Association
sources.relevance: Recommended Practices for the Use of Manually Operated High-Pressure Waterjetting Equipment. Safety data.

Overlap note: steam release → thermal mechanism (burn injury dominates). Explosion/BLEVE → explosion mechanism (blast dominates). Pressure covers the mechanical energy of pressurised fluid/gas without combustion or phase change.

Key insight: hydraulic injection injuries are deceptively serious — the entry wound is a pinhole but the fluid tracks through tissue planes. Many are initially misdiagnosed as minor puncture wounds. Surgical debridement within 6 hours is critical.
